OPENING SUMMARY — WEEK OF SEPTEMBER 14 – 18, 2026

Quantum Computing:

DOE Quantum Genesis Q Competition (DE-FOA-0003657), $215,000,000 across roughly 10 awards, $250,000–$200,000,000, no cost share. A first-of-its-kind effort to build a fault-tolerant, scientifically relevant quantum computer. Domestic commercial entities only — no universities, no nonprofits as leads.

Due October 19, 2026.

Energy / Rural Cooperatives:

USDA Rural Utilities Service Affordable Rural Cooperative (ARC) Energy Program, $175,000,000 in IRA budget authority across roughly 20 awards for advanced transmission and nuclear power supply in rural electric systems. Currently a forecast — estimated post date October 19, 2026. Letters of Interest precede applications.

Natural Resources:

Humanities / Education:

Division of Boating and Waterways 2026 Boating Infrastructure Grant — $18,000,000, $300,000–$1,500,000, 25% match, letter of intent required. Due September 29, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. — this is next week.

grants.Description: U.S. Department of Energy — The Quantum Genesis Q Competition
grants.Opportunity #: DE-FOA-0003657; Assistance Listing 81.049 (Office of Science Financial Assistance Program). Grants.gov opportunity 363869.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Energy — Office of Science. Questions to qcompetition@doe.gov.
grants.Award Range: $250,000 minimum to $200,000,000 maximum. The spread reflects a staged competition structure rather than a single award class — smaller awards fund milestone participation, the ceiling funds buildout of a scientifically relevant quantum computing capability.
grants.Eligible Applicants: Domestic commercial entities only: for-profit organizations other than small businesses, and small businesses.
grants.Program Focus:
Development and deployment of the first fault-tolerant, scientifically relevant quantum computing (SRQC) capability for research and development. The Q Competition is the vehicle for DOE's Quantum Genesis initiative, which DOE describes as a foundational pillar of the broader Genesis Mission and as a step toward the goals in the Executive Order on quantum innovation and its Quantum Computer for Application Development and Discovery Science (QC-ADDS) effort.

DOE frames this as an acceleration mechanism: applicants must present a technically viable plan for hitting the Q Competition milestones. Beyond the first-generation SRQC, DOE signals that selected partners may form the technical foundation for next-generation SRQCs deployed at National Laboratories into the 2030s.
grants.Funding Instrument: Other — a sample Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) is posted with the NOFO. Budget and compliance assumptions built around 2 C.F.R. Part 200 will not transfer cleanly.
grants.Primary Sector: Quantum Computing; Fault-Tolerant Architectures; Quantum Hardware and Software Scaling; Scientific Computing Infrastructure; Other Transactions Authority

grants.Description: USDA Rural Utilities Service — Affordable Rural Cooperative (ARC) Energy Program
grants.Opportunity #: RUS-ARC-2026; Assistance Listing 10.758 (Affordable Rural Cooperative). Grants.gov opportunity 363779.
grants.Agency / Funder: USDA Rural Development — Rural Utilities Service, Electric Program. ARC Help Desk: SM.RD.RUS.ARC-Questions@usda.gov, (202) 690-4492.
grants.Total Funding: $175,000,000 in appropriated budget authority for the cost of loan and grant funds, across approximately 20 awards, under Section 22004 of the Inflation Reduction Act.
grants.Award Range: Up to $20,000,000 maximum; no stated minimum.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Narrow and specific:

• Operating electric cooperatives described in section 501(c)(12) or 1381(a)(2) of the Internal Revenue Code that are current or former RUS electric loan borrowers under the RE Act;

• Electric cooperatives serving predominantly rural areas — defined here as a service territory at least 50% rural; or

• Wholly or jointly owned subsidiaries of such cooperatives.

Investor-owned utilities, municipal utilities, and public power districts are outside this set.
grants.Deadline:
Currently forecast — estimated post date October 19, 2026. No application due date published yet.

The NOFO, Program Guide, sample Letter of Interest, and SF-424 guidance are already posted, so substantive preparation can begin now. RUS is soliciting Letters of Interest first; ARC Applications follow.
grants.Program Focus:
Deployment of advanced, efficient transmission infrastructure and nuclear power supply within rural electric systems, to achieve the emissions reductions contemplated by Section 22004 of the IRA while advancing long-term resiliency, reliability, and affordability.

RUS frames the theory of the case plainly: adding emission-free nuclear supply and increasing transmission grid efficiency reduces future demand for other power sources. Funds are allocated across both purposes.

A New Clean Power Tool workbook is posted as part of the application materials — applicants should expect quantitative modeling to carry real evaluative weight.
grants.Funding Instrument: Other — loans, grants, and loan/grant combinations.
grants.Cost Share / Match:
Yes, and it is structured rather than a flat percentage.

For Project and System loans, RUS finances up to 75% of the total capitalized cost. The awardee must initially provide, and maintain for the term of the award, at least 25% of total capitalized cost as cash or equity investment.

Where financially feasible, RUS may allow the grant component and/or applicable tax credits — including amounts expected through Elective Pay elections under section 6417 of the Internal Revenue Code — to count toward the 25% equity requirement. Equity may not come from loan proceeds from any creditor, including insiders of the awardee.
grants.Primary Sector: Rural Electrification; Transmission Efficiency; Nuclear Power Supply; Inflation Reduction Act Section 22004; Cooperative Finance; Elective Pay / Direct Pay Tax Credits
grants.Link to NOFO: ARC on Simpler.Grants.gov; FY2026 ARC NOFO (PDF); ARC Program Guide, LOI Stage (PDF); RUS ARC program page
grants.Posting Date: Forecast posted September 14, 2026; opportunity last updated September 10, 2026

grants.Description: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service — Cooperative Endangered Species Conservation Fund: Recovery Land Acquisition Grant Program
grants.Opportunity #: F26AS00030; Assistance Listing 15.615 (Cooperative Endangered Species Conservation Fund). Grants.gov opportunity 363856.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. Contact Kelly Niland, Kelly_Niland@fws.gov.
grants.Award Range: $10,000 minimum to $14,162,000 maximum — the ceiling is the full program amount, so a single exceptional acquisition could in principle consume the round.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
State and territorial agencies only, and only those that have entered into a cooperative agreement under section 6(c) of the Endangered Species Act and have provided the information necessary for annual renewal (reconfirmation) of that agreement.

Counties, land trusts, and conservation organizations can participate — but only as subgrantees working with a State agency that holds a cooperative agreement.
grants.Deadline: November 20, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET. Submission is through GrantSolutions.gov, not Grants.gov. Archive date November 27, 2026.
grants.Program Focus:
Acquisition of specific parcels — fee simple or conservation easement — in support of FWS-approved recovery plans and outlines. The program dates to FY2001 and is built on State–Federal cooperation in listed-species conservation.

Requirements that will shape the application:

• Projects must support at least one listed species' most recent FWS-approved recovery planning document in which habitat loss is identified as a threat and habitat protection as a priority recovery action.

• Parcels must be individually identified and sufficiently described for merit review, though they may be grouped at the property or transaction level.

• Applications must include a commitment to fund and implement management of the land in perpetuity consistent with the species' conservation needs.

• A property may not be submitted under both this program and the Habitat Conservation Plan Land Acquisition Grant Program in the same fiscal year.

• Neither the grant nor the non-Federal cost share may be used to satisfy ESA regulatory requirements — Section 7 biological opinions, Section 10 HCP mitigation or monitoring, or any other Federal regulatory mitigation obligation such as Clean Water Act permit mitigation.

• Applications may not be submitted to cover administrative costs alone.
grants.Cost Share / Match: 25% cost share. Pre-award costs may be reimbursable in limited circumstances where necessary to comply with the proposed period of performance, but only if the grant is awarded and only with written approval of the awarding agency (2 C.F.R. 200.458).
grants.Primary Sector: Endangered Species Recovery; Land Acquisition; Conservation Easements; Habitat Protection; State–Federal Cooperative Agreements

grants.Description: NOAA Climate Program Office — FY2026 Earth System Science and Services Partnership (ESSSP)
grants.Opportunity #: NOAA-OAR-CPO-2026-33326; Assistance Listing 11.431 (Climate and Atmospheric Research). Grants.gov opportunity 363852.
grants.Agency / Funder: NOAA Office of Oceanic and Atmospheric Research — Climate Program Office. Point of contact Todd Christenson, Program Manager, (301) 734-1229, todd.christenson@noaa.gov.
grants.Total Funding: Approximately $10,000,000 anticipated for the ESSSP. The listing shows a single expected award with a $10,000,000 ceiling.
grants.Award Range: Up to $10,000,000 for one award. This is effectively a winner-take-all competition, not a portfolio solicitation.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Academic institutions of higher learning that offer doctoral degrees in NOAA-related sciences; consortia of such institutions; or nonprofit research institutions.

Multi-institution applications will not be accepted. A consortium must apply as a consortium, not as several institutions filing together — that distinction is worth confirming with the program officer before structuring a team.
grants.Program Focus:
Research, programs, and projects related to NOAA's mission, carried out primarily through collaboration among scientists and professionals in areas of mutual interest — understanding and predicting changes in the Earth's atmosphere, oceans, coasts, land, and ice, and the interrelated effects on ecosystems, weather and hazards, and communities and infrastructure.

Named collaboration areas: research and analysis; observations and monitoring; data impact evaluations; numerical modeling; and service development and stakeholder engagement.

The breadth here is the point. A partnership award of this size and duration functions as a standing vehicle for NOAA-aligned work rather than a single defined project, which makes the institutional capacity narrative at least as important as any one science aim.
grants.Funding Instrument: Cooperative agreement — expect substantial NOAA involvement in direction and redirection of the technical work.
grants.Cost Share / Match: No cost share or matching requirement.
grants.Primary Sector: Climate and Atmospheric Research; Earth System Modeling; Ocean and Coastal Observation; Weather and Hazards; Stakeholder Engagement and Service Development

grants.Description: National Endowment for the Humanities — Landmarks of American History and Culture and Summer Institutes
grants.Opportunity #: 20261209-EDK-EDU; Assistance Listing 45.039 (NEH: Institutes and Landmarks of American History and Culture). Grants.gov opportunity 363880.
grants.Agency / Funder: National Endowment for the Humanities — Division of Lifelong Learning, 400 Seventh Street SW, Washington, DC 20506. Contact learning@neh.gov.
grants.Award Range: $1 minimum to $460,000 maximum. The $1 floor is a listing artifact; the operative figure is the $460,000 ceiling.
grants.Eligible Applicants: Nonprofits with 501(c)(3) status (non-higher-education); public, state, and private institutions of higher education; state, county, city or township, and special district governments; and federally recognized Native American tribal governments.
grants.Program Focus:
Support for humanities education through professional development for K–12 teachers and higher education faculty. The program combines two long-running NEH lines: Landmarks of American History and Culture, which is place-based and convenes participants at historically significant sites, and Summer Institutes, which are subject-based intensives.

Both the program NOFO and the NEH General Application Guide for Awards to Organizations are posted, so the full requirement set is available now — almost three months of runway.
grants.Cost Share / Match: No cost sharing or matching requirement.
grants.Primary Sector: Humanities Education; K–12 Professional Development; Higher Education Faculty Development; Place-Based Learning; Historic and Cultural Sites
grants.Link to NOFO: Landmarks and Institutes on Simpler.Grants.gov; December 2026 NOFO (PDF); NEH General Application Guide (PDF); NEH Division of Lifelong Learning

grants.Description: California Department of Parks and Recreation, Division of Boating and Waterways — 2026 Boating Infrastructure Grant
grants.Opportunity #: GFO-26-302. Energy Research and Development Division, Food Production Investment Program. Status: active.
grants.Agency / Funder: California Energy Commission. The solicitation manual names the Commission Agreement Officer; the CEC directs all contact through that officer.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
This solicitation is open to all existing food processing and related support facilities located in California. The prime applicant must operate the food-processing facility in which grant-funded equipment will be installed.

For this program, applicants must be existing food processing facilities that are defined by the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS)8 codes:

· 311 (Food Manufacturing),

· 3121 (Beverage Manufacturing),

· 493120 (Refrigerated Warehousing and Storage), and

· 115114 (Postharvest Crop Activities [except Cotton Ginning]).

· Additional NAICS codes may be added via an addendum to the solicitation.9

The following entities are among those that are not eligible to serve as prime applicants for projects under this solicitation:

· Public and private universities

· National labs

· Local publicly owned utilities, investor-owned utilities, or energy service providers

· Equipment manufacturers and vendors

· Design and engineering subcontractors

· M&V subcontractors

· Energy aggregators or developers

· New-build facilities (even those under eligible NAICS codes)

· Multiple different eligible entities (not under the same ownership)

This program is looking for applicants with clear intentions and a build-ready path forward to implementing the technology(ies) listed under Section II.B.2 in California, as demonstrated by the responses in the Project Narrative.
grants.Deadline:
December 17, 2026 at 11:59 p.m.

Questions deadline October 5, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Pre-application workshop September 28, 2026, 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., remote access only.
grants.Program Focus:
Implementation and demonstration of advanced energy and decarbonization technologies in food processing and supporting facilities, targeting commercially available and proven technologies that maximize greenhouse gas emissions reductions, lower energy consumption, and enhance electrical grid reliability.

Note the emphasis on commercially available and proven technology. This is a deployment solicitation, not an R&D solicitation — a client pitching a first-of-a-kind installation is likely in the wrong CEC program.

Full attachment set is posted: solicitation manual, application submittal checklist, project overview form, project narrative, scope of work, project schedule, budget form, CEQA compliance form, commitment and support letters, benefits calculator, and applicant declarations.

A CEQA compliance form is part of the package — for facility installations this is worth scoping early rather than treating as a closeout item.
grants.Funding Instrument: Grant Funding Opportunity. Applications must be submitted through the new Energy Commission Agreement Management System (ECAMS) portal, which requires a user account. CEC has posted user registration instructions and an applying-for-a-solicitation guide.
grants.Primary Sector: Food Processing; Industrial Decarbonization; Energy Efficiency Retrofits; Industrial Heat Pumps; Grid Reliability; California Climate Investments
grants.Link to Solicitation: GFO-26-302 solicitation page; Solicitation Manual (DOCX); Pre-Application Workshop, September 28; ECAMS portal

grants.Description: National Fish and Wildlife Foundation — 2027 Acres for America Request for Proposals
grants.Opportunity #: No federal opportunity number — this is a private foundation RFP administered through NFWF's Easygrants system.
grants.Agency / Funder: National Fish and Wildlife Foundation, in partnership with Walmart. General questions to Dani Tinnin, Manager, Rocky Mountain Regional Office, dani.tinnin@nfwf.org.
grants.Total Funding: Not stated as a program total. NFWF expects to award approximately 5 to 10 grants this cycle.
grants.Award Range: $250,000 to $1,000,000, depending on project scope, conservation value, and readiness. Projects may run up to three years, with acknowledged flexibility for real estate timelines. Start dates should be no later than six months after award announcement.
grants.Eligible Applicants: Nonprofit 501(c) organizations, state government agencies, local and municipal governments, tribal governments and organizations, and educational institutions.
grants.Deadline:
Pre-proposals due October 19, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET.

Applicant webinar September 29, 2026, 3:00–4:00 p.m. ET. Invitations for full proposals sent beginning of November 2026. Full proposals due December 2, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET. Review December 2026 through March 2027; awards announced March 2027.

NFWF strongly encourages contacting the appropriate regional office before submitting a pre-proposal. Western Region: Jonathan Birdsong, jonathan.birdsong@nfwf.org.
grants.Program Focus:
Permanent conservation of large-scale habitat through voluntary land acquisitions and perpetual conservation easements. Launched in 2005, the program has helped protect more than 2 million acres and contributed to connectivity across over 48 million acres of public and private conservation lands.

Four program priorities, with preferential consideration for proposals addressing more than one: conserve critical habitats for birds, fish, plants, and wildlife; connect existing protected lands to unify wild places and protect migration routes; provide public access to the outdoors; and ensure the future of local economies dependent on forestry, ranching, wildlife, and recreation.

What actually drives competitiveness: project scale and strategic importance for the region; endorsement by federal, state, and local agencies that the acquisition is of high conservation value; alignment with published conservation plans, State Wildlife Action Plans, or ESA recovery plans; quantified species benefit; demonstrated threat of conversion; and a fully explained transaction structure including purchase price, seller, buyer, and long-term manager.

Grant funds may only be applied to the property's purchase price. Transaction costs, stewardship endowments, and staff time have to come from match or other sources. Full proposals additionally require digital shapefiles delineating the land in the context of adjacent protected lands.

NFWF requires specific perpetuity language in the grant agreement and land use records, and the fee transfer or easement must qualify for conservation purposes under Internal Revenue Code section 170(h).
grants.Funding Instrument: Foundation grant, primarily reimbursable. Advances require imminent need of expenditure with justification and timeline; monthly advances are not considered.
grants.Cost Share / Match:
Minimum 1:1 match of cash or contributed goods and services. Both federal and non-federal funds may count. All matching sources must be listed regardless of status — intend to apply, submitted, pledged, or received.

Due to the competitive nature of the program, successful Acres for America projects typically carry match at 5:1 or greater. A bare 1:1 application is technically compliant and practically uncompetitive.
grants.Primary Sector: Land Conservation; Conservation Easements; Habitat Connectivity; Public Access; Working Lands Economies; Corporate Conservation Partnership
grants.Link to Solicitation: 2027 Acres for America RFP page; Full RFP (PDF); Applicant Tip Sheet (PDF); Acres for America program page

grants.Description: National Science Foundation and University of Central Florida — National Commercialization and Translation Institute (NCTI)
grants.Opportunity #: No solicitation number yet. NCTI operates under NSF Award No. 2631575 to the University of Central Florida. The solicitation document has not been released — the NCTI mailing list is currently the only notification route.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. National Science Foundation, Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships (TIP), through the University of Central Florida. PI Dr. Ivan Garibay; questions to Ivan.Garibay@ucf.edu.
grants.Total Funding: $20,000,000 over a two-year national pilot, of which $16,000,000 is Participant Commercialization Support to the cohort.
grants.Award Range: $1,000,000 to $3,750,000 per company, milestone-based and need-sized rather than formula-driven. Cohort of 6 to 8 companies; roughly 12 to 16 finalists are interviewed.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Active or recent NSF SBIR/STTR Phase II/IIB awardees with deep-technology innovations.

This is the narrowest eligibility in this digest. A client without an NSF Phase II or IIB award is out, full stop. NCTI states that every eligible awardee may apply and any meritorious company may be funded.

The program deliberately targets companies with high technology readiness but low commercial and investment readiness — the post-SBIR gap where capital-intensive deep tech stalls.
grants.Deadline:
Applications open October 20, 2026; close December 15, 2026.

Finalist interviews January 2027; cohort announced February 2027. The open application window is eight weeks.
grants.Program Focus:
Moving federally funded deep-tech innovations from laboratory to market. NCTI cites that only about one in five Phase II projects has historically produced products or services still in active use.

Selected companies receive a milestone-based commercialization award covering development and non-R&D commercialization work that research grants cannot fund; diagnostic triage across technical development, market validation, business formation, regulatory status, and capital readiness; an Individualized Commercialization Plan co-developed with a senior program advisor; a dedicated mentor team with checkpoint reviews at 90 days, 6 months, and 12 months; brokered access to industry partners, research universities, and national laboratories including Oak Ridge, Sandia, and Pacific Northwest; and curated investor introductions culminating in an annual investor showcase.

Selection is rubric-driven and published in advance. Applications include a technology overview, market assessment, team profile, and draft commercialization plan, evaluated through administrative screening, technical review, and commercial viability assessment against a weighted quantitative rubric anchored to TRL, MRL, CRL, and IRL readiness scales. An independent Selection Board of active investors, industry experts, and entrepreneurs scores every application.

Applicants should understand they are enrolling in a study. NCTI is designed as a national field study with a protocol registered on the Open Science Framework, independent external evaluation by RTI International, and a national longitudinal registry with 12–24 month follow-ups. Every applicant — not only the funded cohort — is scored on the published rubric and enrolled in that registry. Datasets, codebooks, and analysis code are released publicly. Clients sensitive about competitive information should read the eventual solicitation's data terms closely.
grants.Funding Instrument: Participant Commercialization Support award under an NSF cooperative agreement to UCF, with 100% milestone-verified disbursement.
grants.Cost Share / Match: Not stated; the solicitation has not been released.
grants.Primary Sector: Deep Tech Commercialization; SBIR/STTR Phase II/IIB; Investor Readiness; Technology Translation; NSF TIP Directorate; Innovation Policy Research
grants.Link to Solicitation: NCTI program site; NCTI application page; Mailing list — solicitation release notification; NSF and UCF launch announcement
grants.Posting Date: Program announced September 2026; applications open October 20, 2026

grants.Description: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development — FY2026/2027 Community Compass Technical Assistance and Capacity Building Program
grants.Opportunity #: PDR-2600-DC-0006; Assistance Listing 14.259 (Community Compass Technical Assistance and Capacity Building). Grants.gov opportunity 363878.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development — Office of Technical Assistance. Contact communitycompass@hud.gov.
grants.Total Funding: Up to $86,000,000 in 2026 funding, across approximately 45 awards.
grants.Award Range: $250,000 minimum to $35,000,000 maximum — a very wide spread, which in practice means both niche topical providers and full-spectrum TA shops are being solicited under one notice.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Broad: for-profits other than small businesses; nonprofits with and without 501(c)(3) status; state, county, city or township, and special district governments; public and Indian housing authorities; public, state, and private institutions of higher education; and other entities.

HUD specifically names HSIs, HBCUs, TCCUs, Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian-serving institutions, and U.S. territories or possessions.

Individuals, foreign entities, and sole proprietorships are not eligible.
grants.Deadline:
Currently a forecast. Estimated post date November 5, 2026; estimated application due date February 3, 2027; estimated award date April 15, 2027; estimated project start May 15, 2027.

No application documents are posted yet.
grants.Program Focus:
Competitive TA grants under which recipients deliver technical assistance to the people and organizations HUD serves — developing training tools and products, working directly with communities to improve systems and processes, assessing audiences to design fitting curricula, partnering with HUD on urgent high-priority projects, and serving as a thought partner in identifying needs.

HUD is unusually direct about performance expectations. The notice states that recipients failing to meet CCTA's high performance standards will not succeed, that HUD may monitor performance, and that HUD may end an award under 2 C.F.R. 200.340. Applicants must show knowledge of HUD programs and experience carrying them out, staff experienced in designing and delivering training, enough bench depth to shift quickly to high-priority tasks, and the systems and staffing to manage a federal award.

Recipients work with HUD program office leadership on each engagement, receive training and support from HUD's Office of Technical Assistance, and coordinate with other award recipients.
grants.Cost Share / Match: No cost sharing or matching requirement.
grants.Primary Sector: Housing; Community Development; Technical Assistance and Capacity Building; Curriculum Design and Training Delivery; Federal Award Management
grants.Link to NOFO: Community Compass on Simpler.Grants.gov; HUD Community Compass program page; Grants.gov listing
